newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel office critical of CLT-Kirch tie.
newsitem.headline: German cartel office critical of CLT-Kirch tie.

text.p: German cartel authorities said on Monday they take a critical view of a plan by CLT-UFA and the Kirch Group for a 50-50 split of German pay-TV broadcaster Premiere.
Cartel Office spokeswoman Elke Zeise said it was problematical that Germany's only two vendors in the pay-TV market planned to increase their cooperation.
"That could cement the market relationships and make access more difficult for other vendors," she said.

European cartel authorities are likely to be responsible for deciding the case, however, given the scale of the partners' operations and the fact that Bertelsmann makes less than two-thirds of its European sales in Germany, she said.

CLT-UFA, which holds 37.5 percent of Premiere, and Kirch which owns 25 percent, said France's Canal-Plus, which holds the remaining 37.5 percent was satisfied with the deal. But Canal-Plus has so far declined to comment.
